input.title: The Intersection of Crypto-Assets and Money Laundering: Theoretical and Practical Challenges in the EU and UK
input.abstract: This paper examines the criminal law implications of crypto-assets with a focus on money laundering. It first clarifies the technological and economic features of decentralised cryptocurrencies—using Bitcoin as a paradigm—and maps how pseudonymity and mixers shape placement, layering and integration. It then compares the EU and UK AML frameworks (MiCAR, the Single Rulebook and AMLA; MLRs and the 2023 ECCT Act), highlighting their preventive logic. Turning to substantive offences, the paper challenges the UK and Italian approaches on three issues: whether crypto-assets qualify as ‘criminal property’; whether crypto-transactions can conceal illicit origin; and the potential liability of crypto-asset service providers. The analysis reveals a structural asymmetry: while AML regulation advances towards supranational harmonisation, the criminalisation of crypto-laundering—deeply contingent on domestic legal traditions—remains resistant to convergence. The conclusion proposes a calibrated response centred on functional interpretation, refined evidentiary standards, and supervisory guidance rather than legislative expansion. © Enrico Basile, 2026.
